channel.title: Food Safety Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Food Safety Magazine (food-safety.com)

item.title: EU Report Outlines Food Chemical Risk Assessment Data Gaps
item.description: With the goal of supporting stronger risk assessments to address emerging food chemical risks, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) reviewed existing data sources; data gaps and challenges; and recommendations for improving data availability, quality, and interoperability.

item.title: PTNPA Expands 2026 Food Safety Series with Additional Event in Georgia
item.description: The educational series comprises four distinct food safety events taking place across the U.S. to help address the nut industry’s diverse challenges through networking, professional development, and knowledge-sharing.

item.title: EU Increases Import Controls for the Ingredient Behind Global Infant Formula Recall
item.description: Arachidonic acid oil (AHA oil) from a Chinese supplier was identified as the source of cereulide toxin contamination in infant formula produced by Nestlé and other well-known brands. Imports of Chinese AHA oil are now subject to stricter EU border checks.

item.title: ByHeart Infant Formula Botulism Outbreak Ends with Extensive WGS Evidence, but Root Cause Remains Unidentified
item.description: FDA has declared the outbreak over with 48 confirmed and probable cases of illness. A root-cause investigation is still ongoing. FDA has also announced new “Operation Stork Speed” infant formula resources for families.

item.title: Sustainability with ROI: A Beverage Producer Case Study in Water Savings
item.description: Today, food processors face the dual challenge of achieving sustainability goals and guaranteeing product safety.

item.title: Closing the Transparency Gap: FSQA Strategies for Navigating Natural Flavor and Color Regulations
item.description: In light of changing regulations and consumer demand for cleaner labels, this article explores the evolving science, gaps in regulation, and food safety and quality strategies needed to safeguard brands, achieve compliance, and develop the next generation of transparent food systems.

item.title: Study Shows How Allergenic Food Powders Spread During Production, Create Cross-Contamination Risk
item.description: Dispersibility may be a useful tool for simulating the spread and hygienic control of allergenic food powders. Researchers recommend that producers add powders from as low a position as possible to reduce the risk of cross-contamination.

item.title: EU Considers Adoption of Harmonized Precautionary Allergen Labeling Rules
item.description: Following Codex recommendations for risk-based allergen Precautionary Allergen Labeling (PAL) and thresholds, the European Commission has posted a forthcoming draft act to its public feedback portal on harmonized requirements for the use of voluntary PAL statements.

item.title: FDA Funds Penn State Researchers to Continue Wastewater Monitoring for Foodborne Pathogens
item.description: The scientists will isolate and identify pathogens like Salmonella enterica and Listeria monocytogenes from Pennsylvania wastewater using whole genome sequencing (WGS), then work with the State Department of Health to connect isolates to foodborne illness outbreaks.

item.title: Researchers Develop Affordable, Scalable Mushroom-Based Food Packaging
item.description: Unlike plastic, the mycelium- and cellulose-based material is biodegradable and free of chemicals of concern. It is likely safe for humans and the environment in the long term, as demonstrated by humanity’s history of consuming fungi.
